newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tens of thousands march in Paris for education.
newsitem.headline: Tens of thousands march in Paris for education.

text.p: Tens of thousands of school students, parents and teachers marched through Paris in a carnival atmosphere on Sunday demanding more aid for education and protesting at high youth unemployment.

"All together", "Against economic horror" the demonstrators chanted as they marched from the Opera in central Paris to the eastern edge of the capital, to the music of bands and carrying banners and balloons.
About one in four people in France aged under 25 is without a job, double the national average, despite President Jacques Chirac's pledges of a war for jobs when he came to power in 1995.
"Promises to win power -- we're waiting!" banners said in the latest sign of discontent with the centre-right government.

Striking junior hospital doctors were also due to march in cities around France later on Sunday against health care curbs that the government says are vital to enable France to qualify for a planned single European currency from 1999.
Doctors scaled the chimney of a crematorium in Marseille to unfurl a giant banner saying "strike" on Saturday.

Two weeks ago, Chirac called for a drive to equip all French secondary schools with computers by the year 2000 and to eradicate illiteracy as part of a drive to bolster education and boost youth employment.
"The president is responding to the expectations of the young," Labour Minister Jacques Barrot told the weekly Journal du Dimanche. "He wants a more dynamic France where the young find their place."
The young "would be a sacrificed generation if we failed to reform this country," he said.
